ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: From a Kid to a Champion

fullPassage:
[From a Kid to a Champion]

My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogota, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf. But there were a couple of more steep slopes ahead, and I doubted we had a chance. Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!"

Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line."

Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose. The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes. He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."

For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.

[Partners Matter]

While it is true that individual skills are the most important in the world of sports, having a partner who can cooperate with the player with those skills is equally important. In a marathon, a key reason a front runner can reach the finish line after that long journey is the presence of a pacemaker. The pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for the front runner, shielding the front runner from the headwind. Without the pacemaker, the front runner has to cope with the harsh wind alone and put in extra effort to maintain the pace. In Formula One, the world's largest car race series, each team enters two cars. Both drivers try their best for victory, but for the team's win, one person employs strategies such as blocking or obstructing other vehicles so that their teammate can get ahead. In rock climbing, individual skills are essential, but when a mistake is made, the person referred to as the belay partner manages the rope to prevent a fall. Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers are paired up with a dive companion called a "buddy." The buddies are responsible for each other's safety. No matter how exceptional your skills may be, you cannot do it alone.

questions.passage: __FULL__
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안에서 어법상 알맞은 것끼리 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
My parents named me this because they wanted me Ⓐ[to be / being] faster than anyone else. ··· When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race Ⓑ[was held / held] in our small town. ··· Ⓒ[Excited / Exciting] by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever.

det.ref:
[원문] ...wanted me to be faster / a race was held / Excited by what he said
[해석] 나를 가장 빠르게 / 경주가 개최되었다 / 그가 한 말에 신이 난 [문장 02·05·11]
det.correct: Ⓐ want+O+to-V 구조이므로 to be가 적절. Ⓑ 자전거 경주는 개최"되는" 것이므로 수동태 was held. Ⓒ 주어(I)가 감정을 느끼는 대상이므로 과거분사 Excited.
wrongs: ② ❌ being은 want 목적격보어로 부적절, held는 능동태
det.tip:
💡 핵심 문법: 감정분사
• -ed: 감정을 느끼는 주체 (사람)
• -ing: 감정을 유발하는 원인 (사물)
• excited by = ~에 의해 신이 난

⚠️ 함정: 분사구문의 주어와 주절 주어가 일치하는지 확인!

ch: ① to be – was held – Exciting
③ to be – was held – Excited

questions.passage: __FULL__
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안에서 어법상 알맞은 것끼리 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
He brought me into his professional team, Ⓐ[where / which] only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. ··· He had a lot of experience in Ⓑ[riding / to ride] on hills and mountains.

det.ref:
[원문] ...his professional team, where only... / experience in riding
[해석] 그의 프로 팀으로, 그곳에서… / 타는 것에 대한 경험 [문장 15·20]
det.correct: Ⓐ 선행사 team은 "장소"이므로 관계부사 where 적절. Ⓑ 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(riding)가 와야 함.
wrongs: ① ❌ to ride는 전치사 뒤에 올 수 없음
② ❌ which는 관계대명사로 뒤에 불완전한 절이 와야 하는데, came together는 완전한 절
det.tip:
💡 where vs which
• where: 선행사가 장소 + 뒤에 완전한 절
• which: 선행사가 사물 + 뒤에 불완전한 절

⚠️ 전치사 + 동명사: in/on/at/of + V-ing

questions.passage: Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel ______ in first place, and our team would have won.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place.
[해석] 내가 넘어지지 않았더라면, Gabriel이 1위를 했을 텐데. [문장 34]
det.correct: 가정법 과거완료: If+S+had p.p., S+would have p.p. 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하므로 would have come이 정답.
wrongs: ① ❌ would come은 가정법 과거(현재 반대)
det.tip:
💡 가정법 과거완료
• If + S + had p.p., S + would/could have p.p.
• 과거에 일어나지 않은 일을 가정

⚠️ 혼합 가정법에 주의: If절(과거완료) + 주절(가정법 과거) 가능

questions.passage: Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember ______ finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you."
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone.
[해석] 나는 네가 모두를 2바퀴 앞서 결승선을 통과한 것을 기억한다. [문장 40]
det.correct: 동명사(finishing)의 의미상 주어는 소유격(your)이 문법적으로 올바름. 구어체에서는 you도 가능하나, 격식체/시험에서는 소유격 your이 정답.
wrongs: ② ❌ 구어체에서 가능하나 문법적으로 소유격이 원칙
③ ❌ yours는 소유대명사로 뒤에 명사 불가
④ ❌ yourself는 재귀대명사로 의미상 주어 불가
⑤ ❌ you are finishing은 동명사가 아닌 진행형
det.tip:
💡 동명사의 의미상 주어
• 격식: 소유격 + V-ing (your finishing)
• 비격식: 목적격 + V-ing (you finishing)
• remember + V-ing: 과거에 한 일을 기억

⚠️ remember to V vs remember V-ing 구별!

questions.passage: He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he ______ me as "kid."
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid."
[해석] 그가 나를 "꼬마"라고 부르지 않은 것은 처음이었다. [문장 52]
det.correct: It was the first time + 주어 + had p.p. 구문. 과거 시점까지의 경험을 나타내므로 과거완료 had not addressed.
wrongs: ① ❌ 단순 과거는 the first time 구문에 부적절
③ ❌ 현재완료는 It is the first time에 사용
det.tip:
💡 the first time 구문
• It is the first time + S + has/have p.p.
• It was the first time + S + had p.p.
• 시제 일치에 주의!

⚠️ is/was에 따라 완료 시제가 달라짐!

questions.passage: When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team. I felt small and ( ______ ).
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 13자, i로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] I felt small and insignificant.
[해석] 나는 작고 하찮게 느꼈다. [문장 16]
det.correct: insignificant: 하찮은, 중요하지 않은. 프로 팀에서 자신이 보잘것없다고 느낀 감정을 표현.
det.tip:
💡 insignificant 어휘
• in-(부정) + significant(중요한) = 하찮은
• 유의어: trivial, unimportant, negligible
• 반의어: significant, important, meaningful

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 모두 찾아 바르게 고친 것은?
I could sprint the Ⓐfaster on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I Ⓑhave rarely cycled up steep slopes Ⓒago. Gabriel was from Bogota, Colombia, Ⓓwhich is high up in the Andes.

det.ref:
[원문] I could sprint the fastest / I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before / which is high up
[해석] 가장 빨리 달릴 수 있었다 / 가파른 경사를 거의 타본 적이 없었다 [문장 17-19]
det.correct: Ⓐ the+최상급이므로 faster→fastest. Ⓑ 과거 이전의 경험이므로 have→had (과거완료). Ⓒ 과거완료와 함께 ago→before 사용.
wrongs: ⑤ ❌ Ⓓ which는 보충 설명 계속적 용법으로 적절, ⒷⒸ 누락
det.tip:
💡 ago vs before
• ago: 현재 기준 (과거시제와 사용)
• before: 과거 기준 (과거완료와 사용)
• three years ago (O) / had ... before (O)

⚠️ 과거완료 + ago는 시험 빈출 오류!

questions.passage: ( ______ ) by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones.
questions.stem: 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오: motivate (1단어, 영문 9자, M으로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses.
[해석] Gabriel의 격려에 동기를 부여받아, 나는 모든 훈련 코스에 열심히 참가했다. [문장 22]
det.correct: 주어(I)가 동기를 "부여받는" 대상이므로 과거분사 Motivated. 분사구문에서 수동 의미.
det.tip:
💡 분사구문의 능동/수동
• 능동: V-ing ~, S + V (주어가 행위자)
• 수동: p.p. ~, S + V (주어가 대상)
• Motivated by = Being motivated by

⚠️ Motivating vs Motivated: 주어가 동기를 주는지/받는지 구별!

questions.passage: Soon after, my efforts finally <u>paid off</u> in one of the mountain courses.
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 paid off의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses.
[해석] 얼마 지나지 않아, 나의 노력이 마침내 산악 코스 중 하나에서 성과를 거두었다. [문장 23]
det.correct: pay off: (노력·투자가) 성과를 거두다, 보람이 있다. 여기서는 꾸준한 훈련의 결과가 나왔다는 의미.
wrongs: ② ❌ pay off a debt(빚을 갚다)와 다른 의미
④ ❌ 해고의 의미는 be laid off
det.tip:
💡 pay off의 다의어
• (노력이) 성과를 거두다: Hard work pays off.
• (빚을) 갚다: pay off a loan
• 문맥에서 의미를 판단!

⚠️ pay off vs pay for vs pay back 구별!

questions.passage: As a domestique, I was riding in front of Gabriel ( ______ ) him from the headwind.
questions.stem: 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오: shield (1~2단어, 영문 9자, t로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind.
[해석] 나는 Gabriel 앞에서 그를 역풍으로부터 보호하기 위해 달리고 있었다. [문장 24]
det.correct: to shield: ~하기 위해 (목적의 to부정사 부사적 용법). 앞에서 달린 목적이 역풍 차단임.
det.tip:
💡 to부정사 부사적 용법 (목적)
• ~하기 위해: to V = in order to V = so as to V
• shield A from B: A를 B로부터 보호하다

⚠️ shielding도 분사구문으로 가능하나, 원문은 to shield

questions.passage: I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "<u>You</u> outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 You가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] You outran the others by two laps!
[해석] 너는 다른 선수들을 2바퀴나 앞섰어! [문장 13]
det.correct: Gabriel이 어린 Bliksem에게 한 말. 1위로 들어온 Bliksem을 칭찬하며 "You"라고 부름.
wrongs: ④ ❌ 다른 선수들은 the others로 지칭됨
det.tip:
💡 지칭추론 전략
• 대화 상황에서 화자(speaker)와 청자(listener) 구별
• 앞뒤 문맥에서 행위자 확인
• 대명사가 가리키는 대상의 행동과 역할 매칭

questions.passage: I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his ( ______ ).
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 6자, b로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] He urged me to continue on his behalf.
[해석] 그는 나에게 자기 대신 계속하라고 촉구했다. [문장 29]
det.correct: on one's behalf: ~를 대신하여, ~를 위하여. Gabriel이 부상으로 계속할 수 없어 Bliksem에게 대신 달리라고 함.
det.tip:
💡 on one's behalf
• on behalf of + 사람: ~를 대신하여
• on my/his/her behalf: 나/그/그녀를 대신하여
• 유의어: instead of, in place of

questions.passage: I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place. ( ______ ), Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it."
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 12자, S로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug.
[해석] 놀랍게도, Gabriel은 나에게 부드러운 포옹을 해 주었다. [문장 35]
det.correct: Bliksem은 사고를 낸 것에 죄책감을 느꼈는데, 예상과 달리 Gabriel이 포옹하며 격려함. 반전/예상 밖의 상황이므로 Surprisingly(놀랍게도).
det.tip:
💡 부사 연결어
• 예상 밖: Surprisingly, Unexpectedly
• 역접: However, Nevertheless
• 추가: Moreover, Furthermore
• 결과: Consequently, Therefore

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 영어로 올바르게 옮긴 것은?
나는 좀 더 조심했어야 했다.

det.ref:
[원문] I should have been more careful.
[해석] 나는 좀 더 조심했어야 했다. [문장 33]
det.correct: "~했어야 했다"는 과거의 후회/유감을 나타내는 should have p.p. 구문.
wrongs: ③ ❌ had to be는 과거의 의무(사실)
det.tip:
💡 should have p.p.
• 과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 후회
• I should have studied harder. (더 열심히 공부했어야 했는데)
• You should not have said that. (그런 말 하지 말았어야 했는데)

⚠️ should have p.p. vs could have p.p. vs would have p.p. 구별!

ch: ① I must be more careful.
② I should be more careful.
③ I had to be more careful.
④ I should have been more careful.
⑤ I would have been more careful.

questions.passage: As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. ( ______ ), the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue.
questions.stem: 윗글의 빈칸에 알맞은 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 7자, H로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue.
[해석] 그러나, 울퉁불퉁한 자갈길이 타이어 펑크를 일으켜 나는 계속할 수 없었다. [문장 39]
det.correct: 전략에 집중하며 이기고 싶었지만(긍정) → 타이어 펑크(부정). 역접 관계이므로 However.
det.tip:
💡 However vs But
• However: 문장 앞에서 쉼표와 함께 사용 (부사)
• But: 절과 절을 연결 (접속사)
• However는 문장 중간/끝에도 올 수 있음

questions.stem:
다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 모두 찾아 바르게 고친 것은?
Our speed increased as we Ⓐapproaching the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. questions.stem:

When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members Ⓐthat I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride Ⓑfaster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I Ⓒought to be the team leader. I was deeply Ⓓtouching and felt a burden on my shoulders.

det.ref:
[원문] asked the members if I could lead / ride faster than me / insisted that I ought to be / I was deeply touched
[해석] 내가 팀을 이끌 수 있는지 물었다 / 나보다 빠르게 / 내가 팀 리더가 되어야 한다고 주장 / 깊이 감동받았다 [문장 56-58]
det.correct: Ⓐ ask는 의문을 전달하므로 that→if(~인지). Ⓑ 비교급 faster는 적절하지만 ride는 자동사이므로 faster 대신 fast(부사 원급)? 아니, ride faster than me는 비교급으로 적절. 하지만 원문에서 faster는 맞음. 실제로 ride faster는 "더 빠르게 달리다"로 적절. 그런데 여기서 fast→faster 비교급이 맞으므로 Ⓑ은 오류. 아 잠깐, 원문이 "ride faster than me"이니까 faster가 맞음. 그러면 Ⓑ은 정상. Ⓓ 감정을 느끼는 주체이므로 touching→touched.
wrongs: ③ ❌ Ⓐ도 if로 고쳐야 하고, Ⓑ faster는 비교급으로 적절
④ ❌ whether도 가능하나 Ⓓ touching이 아닌 touched가 되어야 함
det.tip:
💡 ask + if/whether
• ask + O + if/whether + S + V: ~인지 물어보다
• ask + O + that절 (X) → that은 의문 전달 불가

⚠️ touching vs touched
• touching: 감동을 주는 (원인)
• touched: 감동을 받은 (경험자)
